title: Token SLI cohorting and probabilistic shedding sandbox
creator: Asha Patel
description: Build a telemetry and visualization sandbox to support token-level SLIs by cohort and to evaluate probabilistic (stochastic) load-shedding policies across regions. The goal is to produce an instrumentation pattern and dashboard that helps engineers and SREs understand how per-token latency distributions vary by customer cohort, prefix patterns, and KV cache effectiveness, and to validate probabilistic shedding as a graceful degradation strategy during regional congestion. This ticket covers: 1) lightweight per-token sampling and cohort attribution without exhaustive token collection; 2) ingest and storage schema for sampled telemetry; 3) a Grafana playground with cohorted P50/P95/P99, KV-hit overlays, and shedding decision traces; and 4) a synthetic-shedding simulator that can run regional failforward scenarios and estimate customer-visible SLO impact.
acceptance_criteria: Sampling: Implement an opt-in per-token sampling hook that annotates requests with cohort_id and prefix_bucket and emits at most 1% of tokens for production traffic (sampling ratio configurable per route).

Storage: Sample payloads are parsable by the analytics pipeline and stored in the telemetry index with fields: timestamp, region, route, cohort_id, token_pos, token_latency_ms, kv_hit, shed_decision, upstream_variant.

Dashboards: Grafana sandbox includes panels for cohorted latency histograms (token-level), KV-hit heatmap by prefix, probabilistic-shed decision rate over time, and a correlation scatter of kv_hit vs per-token latency. Panels support region-filter and time-range linking.

Simulator: A bench harness can inject synthetic traffic to reproduce a regional congestion event and run at least three shedding strategies (fixed-threshold, priority-cohort, probabilistic) and output projected SLO delta for a given cohort mix.
Runbook: Draft runbook section describing how to enable sampling for an org, interpret panels, and conduct an emergency probabilistic-shed rollback.
